author: Sayaka Murata

commentary.text:
Interesting read. This was very different to anything I'd read lately. I appreciated the novel point of view, and thought the author did a good job making me relate to the main character. I understood the frustration with everyone in her life, trying to make her live in a way that was totally unnatural and undesirable to her. 

The male character was a bit odd, and I had hoped for more character growth out of him once they started living together. But, that's probably the point Murata is trying to make. He is who he is, and Keiko is who she is. 

It was a memorable, triumphant moment when she decided to go back to the store in the end.

synopsis:
Thirty-six-year-old Tokyo native Keiko Furukura has always felt like an outsider, struggling to belong throughout her childhood and school years. Everything changes at eighteen when she takes a job at the Hiiromachi Smile Mart. Inside the shop, she finally discovers a sense of clarity and direction. Guided by the explicit instructions in the employee manual and by mimicking the clothing, tone, and habits of the staff around her, she successfully acts the part of an ordinary person. 

While supervisors cycle through over the course of nearly two decades, Keiko remains a fixture at the store, becoming so deeply intertwined with it that her identity and the establishment seem to blur together. Although she is thoroughly content with her routine, her relatives and peers grow increasingly critical of her unmarried status and lack of a traditional profession, eventually driving her to take drastic measures.
title: Convenience Store Woman
